summary.title: Interactive Guide: Mastering Rate Limiting
summary.one_liner: Learn how the four common rate limiting algorithms (token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window counter, sliding window counter) work, using interactive demo apps for each.
takeaways: Rate limiting prevents one user from overusing a resource and protects service quality for others, reduces hosting cost, and gives basic DDoS protection.
Token bucket: tokens refill at a fixed rate and each request consumes one; it allows occasional short bursts.
Leaky bucket: requests queue in a bucket that drains at a constant rate and are dropped when full; it smooths bursts into a steady output.
Fixed window counter is simple and efficient but allows traffic spikes at window boundaries.
Sliding window counter checks a timestamped log of recent requests against a limit over the last X seconds.
summary.summary: This short interactive guide introduces rate limiting for back-end applications and explains its benefits. It describes four common algorithms: token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window counter, and sliding window counter, with a brief working description of each and its trade-offs. The author built a separate interactive app for each algorithm so readers can experiment with them. The page is brief and does not include code or implementation details.
